President Bola Tinubu has directed security agencies to strengthen intelligence sharing and coordination to improve security ahead of the 2027 general elections. The order comes as the Inspector General of Police, Olatunji Disu, ordered the redeployment of 128 senior police officers, comprising 22 Commissioners of Police and 106 Assistant Commissioners of Police, to various departments, formations and commands across the country. On Sunday, the police boss had redeployed 13 Assistant Inspectors-General of Police and two Commissioners of Police. Calling for strengthened intelligence, the President said the measure was necessary to protect vulnerable communities and ensure Nigerians could exercise their democratic rights without fear. Tinubu, represented by a presidential delegate at the opening of the Chief of Defence Intelligence Annual Conference 2026 in Abuja on Monday, said the government would sustain pressure on criminal and terrorist networks. He said closer intelligence sharing among the Department of State Services, Armed Forces, Nigeria Police Force and other security agencies would help consolidate recent operational gains. “Through closer intelligence sharing and coordinated action among the DSS, Armed Forces, police and other security agencies, we will consolidate these gains, sustain pressure on criminal and terrorist networks, protect vulnerable communities and strengthen security ahead of the 2027 general elections,” he said. The President added, “Every Nigerian must be able to live, work and exercise their democratic rights in safety.” Tinubu said the country’s security challenges had become increasingly complex, with threats ranging from terrorism, banditry and kidnapping to cybercrime and transnational organised crime. He noted that four of eight identified senior terrorist leaders had been killed or arrested under his administration. According to him, the achievements included operations against the Islamic State West Africa Province’s southern expansion network, the killing of senior Islamic State leader, Abu Bilal Mainuki, in May 2026, and the arrests of Abu Barra of Ansaru and Mamuda of Mahmudawa in 2025. The President also disclosed that incidents of illegal oil bunkering and vandalism of critical oil and gas installations in the Niger Delta dropped from 32 in the first quarter of 2026 to 17 in the third quarter, representing a 46.88 per cent reduction. He urged security agencies to strengthen their intelligence capabilities through technological innovation, particularly artificial intelligence, machine learning, cyber capabilities and unmanned surveillance systems. Tinubu said the government was also working to modernise the country’s intelligence architecture through strategic partnerships with local and international security institutions. He urged participants at the conference to translate their deliberations into measurable security outcomes, stressing that the ultimate objective was to make communities safer. Tinubu also said security forces have eliminated or arrested four of eight identified top terrorist leaders, including key figures linked to regional extremist networks, with operations ongoing to neutralise the remaining four. He said his administration was strengthening intelligence-driven operations and embracing emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, machine learning and unmanned systems, to combat terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and cybercrime. He said, “Recent operational successes, however, demonstrate our growing capacity to dismantle terrorist leadership, disrupt expansion networks and deny violent groups freedom of action. Operations remain focused on the remaining identified leaders: Ba Shuwa of ISWAP; Abdullahi Oro of IS-Sahel; Sadiku of JAS in the North Central region; and Bakura Doro in the Lake Chad Basin. The security services have also killed senior bandit leaders, including Halilu Sububu, and many of their fighters, sustaining pressure on the networks threatening our communities.” Tinubu said the increasing use of advanced digital tools by criminal groups had made integrated, forward-looking intelligence essential for guiding swift military and security decisions. He disclosed that the Federal Government had introduced a five-year strategic defence operations plan designed to place accurate intelligence at the centre of national security operations. The President reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to leveraging technology and intelligence to address the country’s security challenges, adding that security agencies must sustain operational coordination to protect lives and property ahead of the 2027 elections. He revealed that more than 1,000 convictions had been secured following over 2,000 terrorism-related trials in recent years. He described the development as a significant demonstration of the administration’s commitment to ensuring accountability for terrorism and other security-related crimes. In another development, the police, in two wireless messages dated November 16, 2026, redeployed officers involved in key operational, investigative, administrative and specialised units of the Nigeria Police Force. According to one of the messages, “The IGP has ordered the posting of the following CPs as indicated against their names.” Among the Commissioners of Police affected, Arikpo Ofemi Ikpi was posted to the Special Enquiry Bureau of the Force Criminal Investigation Department Annex in Lagos, while Felix Akoneme Nnebue was deployed to the Anti-Human Trafficking unit in Abuja. Mamman Bitrus Giwa was posted to the Special Enquiry Bureau of the FCID in Abuja, while Charles E. Dike was deployed to the Special Protection Unit at the Force Headquarters. Also, Gazali Alade Abdul-Salaam was posted as Commissioner of Police, Operations, Force Intelligence Department, Abuja, with effect from November 30, 2026. Other commissioners affected include Nelson Nwamana, posted as CP Administration, FCID Annex, Lagos; Nache Bashiru Liman, CP General Investigation, FCID Annex, Kaduna; Emman Adegboyega Oyeleye, CP Interpol, Lagos; and Isiaka Salau Oyenuga, CP Anti-Fraud, FCID Annex, Enugu. Abdulkarim Musa Waziri was posted as CP INEC, Abuja, while Mohammed Yusuf Adamu was deployed as CP Railway. The postings also affected 106 Assistant Commissioners of Police, who were redeployed to various state commands, area commands, Police Mobile Force units and specialised departments. Among them, Rex Abiodun Enwelike was posted to the Ozoro Divisional Training School, while Raji Ganiyu was deployed to Area Command J, Ajah, Lagos. Samuel Ijachi was posted to the 70 Police Mobile Force, Kabba, Kogi State; Mohammed Temitope Ogunrin to the 16 Police Mobile Force, Abeokuta, Ogun State; and Idris Bunu to the 75 Police Mobile Force, Obudu, Cross River State. Other ACPs were deployed to the Force Criminal Investigation Department, State Criminal Investigation Departments, X-Squad, Special Fraud Unit, railway police and various zonal commands. The wireless messages directed the relevant departments and formations to update their records accordingly. The PUNCH had on Monday reported that Disu ordered the posting of 13 Assistant Inspectors-General of Police and two Commissioners of Police to new commands and departments across the country, according to a police wireless message dated November 15.
